keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The Province of Lower Canada was created by the Constitutional Act 1791 from the partition of the British colony'; 'The province covered Labrador until the Labrador region was transferred to Newfoundland in 1809.' The page gives no 1791 area; the gazetteer shape is the St Lawrence region (0.42 M km2) plus the Labrador coastal strip. The Labrador dispute page (opened for the Newfoundland dossier) says Labrador was then 'limited to a coastal strip'. Soft.

ledger.note: 1791: Lower Canada is created. 'The Province of Lower Canada was created by the Constitutional Act 1791 from the partition of the British colony' (infobox 26 December 1791); the Province of Quebec page: 'divided the colony in two at the Ottawa River'.

region.text: the Labrador coast, which the province covered 'until the Labrador region was transferred to Newfoundland in 1809' (a coastal strip, the researcher's reading from the Labrador boundary dispute page)

ledger.note: 1809: Labrador goes to Newfoundland. 'The province covered Labrador until the Labrador region was transferred to Newfoundland in 1809'; the Colony of Newfoundland page: 'In 1809, the British Imperial government detached Labrador from Lower Canada for transfer to the Newfoundland Colony.'

region.text: the Saint Lawrence valley of Quebec: Lower Canada east of the Ottawa River

ledger.note: 1841: Lower Canada is united with Upper Canada. The provinces were 'combined as the United Province of Canada in 1841, when the Act of Union 1840 came into force' (infobox 10 February 1841).

region.text: the Saint Lawrence valley of Quebec: Lower Canada east of the Ottawa River

ledger.note: 1841: the colony is dissolved on 10 February 1841; its territory becomes Canada East.

wars.name: Lower Canada Rebellion
wars.outcome: Rebellions in 1837-38; 'the 1791 Constitution was suspended on 27 March 1838'; no territory changed hands.
wars.note: The page names the rebellions only in the infobox/footnotes; the rebels are not named as a state.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary survey; the border with the United States and with New Brunswick (Maine) was disputed (Webster-Ashburton is not on the page) and the northern limit of the province was never fixed.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row. Pages: Lower Canada, Province of Quebec (1763-1791), Colony of Newfoundland (for the 1809 detachment) (three; the Quebec and Newfoundland pages are cited by the Upper Canada and Newfoundland dossiers' events too). Not on the pages: the Ottawa River boundary with Upper Canada (Quebec page only), seigneuries, the Maine/New Brunswick boundary, Anticosti and the Magdalen Islands beyond the 1809 footnote, the American invasions. The Labrador loss is recorded with the counterpart string dominion-of-newfoundland (written in this batch; it is the Newfoundland Colony of 1809).
